title: Score an ampoule neck and open it while retaining its cap
instruction: Score the neck of the inert ampoule using the abrasive collar, then open it with the captive opener. Keep the body upright and both grippers off the cap and neck. Leave the body in its holder and the cap captured inside the opener on its rack. Release both hands.
context: Ampoules that require filing must have their neck scored before opening. This task isolates scoring, protected opening, and retained-tip handling during medication-container preparation; it uses an inert training replica, without medicine or a patient.
setup: Official bimanual YAM station. Table top z 0.7475 m. x away from robots and y toward the left arm. Ampoule body is an original rigid 12 mm diameter by 40 mm long inert replica with a 6 mm diameter neck. Body mass 8 g. Its root is at x 260 mm and y 20 mm and z 24 mm above the tabletop. Its bottom rests on a 4 mm high holder floor. Cap is 20 mm long with a maximum diameter of 9 mm and mass 1 g. Cap root is at the neck plane z 44 mm above table. A native fixed neck joint has initial unscored break torque 0.20 N m and axial break force 20 N. These are prototype parameters pending physical calibration. The plastic opener has a 24 mm square exterior by 83 mm height and total mass 22 g. Its mouth faces downward. Its root starts at x 280 mm and y negative 140 mm and z 84 mm above table. Four passive retaining jaws move radially up to 3 mm. Each jaw mass is 1 g and its spring is 5000 N per metre with damping 5 N seconds per metre and a 5 N force limit. The light blue ampoule geometry represents an inert glass or rigid polymer replica. The blue tool represents rigid plastic with compliant ring behavior approximated by passive jaws. The fixed body holder has a 13 mm opening and 20 mm outer width and an 8 mm wall height on its 4 mm floor. The fixed opener rack has a 70 mm square base and two 44 mm support ledges that hold the downward mouth clear. All authored solids and joint anchors are listed in scene_inventory.json. No medication or patient or real sharp fragment is used. Four additional radial file shoes each have 0.5 g mass, 500 N/m stiffness, 0.5 N s/m damping, a 1 N force limit, and 3 mm travel. Beveled entry faces yield to the cap during insertion. Their inner edges contact the 6 mm neck. Thirty-six non-colliding visual sectors show measured scoring coverage.
scoring: Before opening, native file-to-neck contact and relative tangential file motion must cover at least 34 of 36 circumferential sectors with at least 0.25 mm travel per sector and 15 mm total travel. This changes the surrogate native neck torque threshold from 0.20 to 0.020 N m. A break before qualification permanently fails. Unscored cap coverage earns at most 0.15. 0.25 after neck qualification when the opener covers the cap before a confirmed joint break. A measured neck gap alone can only earn 0.25 while the cap remains covered. Higher scores require a confirmed native joint break. 0.5 when cap base separation from the body neck is at least 12 mm and the entire cap remains inside the tool cavity but the body or tool is not yet returned. 0.75 for the opened body upright within 5 degrees and within 2 mm of the holder target and the opener within 3 mm and 5 degrees of its rack target before both hands are released. 0.9 once both hands are open beyond 35 mm travel and clear of all movable objects and every physical vertex of the body and cap and opener housing and all eight jaw/file links stays within a 0.50 mm peak excursion bound and every rigid body orientation changes by at most 1 degree over a continuous one second of native substeps. Any excursion or loss of hand clearance or return pose restarts the complete interval. 1.0 after these release conditions hold for one further continuous second. Permanent zero after direct robot contact within 6 mm of the neck or any direct cap contact within 0.20 mm native contact separation. Permanent zero after any body tilt above 15 degrees or any cap escape once the joint breaks or the neck gap exceeds 0.50 mm or any drop below the tabletop by more than 2 mm or any invalid measurement. Cap base must be laterally within 1.5 mm of the tool axis and from 33 to 41 mm below the tool root. All cap mesh vertices must lie within the 12 mm square protective cavity and between 39 mm below and 40 mm above its root. A video and ruler and angle gauge can score the replica. Native normal force above 10 micronewtons gates abrasive contact; grade thresholds use coverage and physical outcomes, not a target force. All other outcomes score zero.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds.
reset_notes: One epoch per process. A neck is consumed and must be replaced in a physical inert replica. In simulation start a fresh process so that the native breakaway joint is restored before physics initialization. Restore the cap and body poses and all eight jaw/file positions and abrasion history. Use seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Native contact drives spring file shoes and retaining jaws. Contact-gated tangential travel weakens a native fixed neck joint from 0.20 to 0.020 N m; PhysX produces breakage. Abrasion and break thresholds are uncalibrated inert-replica parameters. Glass cracks, material removal, fragments, fluids and sterility are omitted. Controller and scorer never write object poses or disable the joint. Clinical effectiveness is unvalidated.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 2400 steps; scripted demo: 1.0 in 782 steps.
